title: Complement cannot also meet the edge bound at eleven vertices
statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ with $n = \abs{V} \ge 11$, write $E(G)$ for its edge set, and let $G^{c}$ be its complement (the simple graph on $V$ in which two distinct vertices are adjacent exactly when they are not adjacent in $G$). Then $G$ and $G^{c}$ cannot both satisfy $\abs{E(G)} + 6 \le 3n$ and $\abs{E(G^{c})} + 6 \le 3n$; that is, at least one of the two graphs has more than $3n - 6$ edges.
